'''Timothy M. Lohman''' (born 1951) earned his [[Ph.D.]] in [[physical chemistry]] from the [[University of Wisconsin-Madison]] in 1977.<ref name="auto1">{{cite web | title=Timothy Lohman, PhD | website=www.siteman.wustl.edu | url=https://www.siteman.wustl.edu/DoctorProfile.aspx?Type=Research&memid=2582 | access-date=2025-11-23}}</ref> After completing his [[Ph.D.]], he furthered his training with [[postdoctoral research]] at the [[University of California]] and the [[University of Oregon]].<ref name="auto1"/> He is currently a professor in the department of [[biochemistry]] and [[molecular biophysics]] at the [[Washington University School of Medicine]].<ref name="auto"/> He has been named to the position of Marvin A. Brennecke Professor of Biological Chemistry<ref name="auto"/> and in 2008 served as president of the [[Gibbs Society of Biological Thermodynamics]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Gibbs Society of Biological Thermodynamics History Page | website=mljohnson.pharm.virginia.edu | url=http://mljohnson.pharm.virginia.edu/gibbs-society/history.html | access-date=2025-11-23}}</ref> 
He will be giving the second annual Gary K. Ackers Lecture at the 24th annual meeting of the [[Gibbs Society of Biological Thermodynamics]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://gibbs.biology.lsu.edu/ |title=The 24th Annual Gibbs Conference on Biothermodynamics |access-date=2010-03-23 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719231743/http://gibbs.biology.lsu.edu/ |archive-date=2011-07-19 }} 2010-03-24</ref>

Lohman's research has centered on obtaining a molecular understanding of the mechanisms of [[protein]]-[[nucleic acid]] interactions involved in [[DNA metabolism]], in particular, DNA [[motor proteins]], such as [[helicases]] and [[translocases]], and single stranded DNA binding proteins. [[thermodynamic]], [[kinetic energy|kinetic]], [[structural]] and single molecule approaches are used by his lab to observe these interactions.

Lohman is married and has two children.
